result.title: Allocation Before the Clock: Graph, Set and Game Theory of Professional League of Legends Objective Setups
result.summary: Before every neutral objective in professional League of Legends, each team decides which of its five players walk to the pit, which hold a lane, and when to commit. The leading analysis of such setups, TAGNet for Counter-Strike 2, clusters graph-network embeddings of player positions and reads cluster win rates as tactical quality. We treat a setup as an allocation on a walled map: formations are set partitions on the lattice $Π_5$, control is a geodesic Voronoi split of a navigation graph, and commitment is an allocation game solved as a quantal response equilibrium priced in win probability. On all 164 games of MSI and Worlds 2025 (2,994 team-setups, minimap tracks validated against Riot positions), trailing teams leave the pit empty far more often than leading teams, by +34.8 percentage points at the first baron and +30.4 percentage points at Atakhan. Our model, HASSE-QRE, finds six setup patterns that whole-model series-bootstrap refits reproduce (ARI 0.819, comparable to 0.813 for TAGNet's $K$-Means step alone) and indicates that teams price fights, travel and committed players, not the objective itself (weight 0.018; fixing it to one costs 59.9 log-likelihood points). The equilibrium reproduces a quarter of the commitment gap, almost all of it through state variables rather than its strategic channels. Weighting a team-level contrast by exposure moves it across $p=0.05$ (0.046 against 0.052). We release the tracks, setups and code.

AI.brief_summary: 该文把职业英雄联盟争夺中立资源前的队伍站位视为有墙地图上的分配问题，用集合划分（Π₅）、导航图上的测地 Voronoi 控制区与量化反应均衡（HASSE-QRE）建模，并在 2025 MSI 与 Worlds 的 164 场比赛中分析领先与落后队伍的投入差异。
AI.relevance_reason: 其量化反应均衡对「是否投入、何时承诺」的噪声化建模，可能为 LVR 中 STOP 决策与证据/计算投入的软性刻画提供概念参照，但论文不涉及模型内部状态或视觉推理，可供核查的线索较间接。
